news.title: Nike Honours Mbappé’s World Cup Legacy With New Signature Mercurial Superfly 11
news.lede: When you're the Golden Boot winner at back-to-back World Cups and the all-time leading goalscorer in tournament history, a standard player edition just isn't going to cut it. So it's only right that Nike has celebrated Kylian Mbappé’s incredible legacy with a brand new signature Mercurial Superfly 11. And yes, as you'd probably expect, it's dripping in gold. Arriving in a striking "Mtlc Gold/Green Glow/White" colourway, Mbappé's latest signature boot takes direct inspiration from the Frenchman's accomplishments on football’s biggest stage.

news.title: World football turns on Infantino as UEFA, AFC and CONCACAF demand review
news.lede: The battle over FIFA's controversial plan to sell a stake linked to the commercial value of the World Cup has escalated into a major governance crisis. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf have jointly accused FIFA leadership of breaking the trust of the football community and called for an independent review of the entire episode.The three confederations issued a strongly worded open letter on Monday, taking aim at the way FIFA president Gianni Infantino and his administration handled the proposal. They rejected FIFA's explanation that the controversy was simply a communication failure and argued that the episode reflected a much deeper problem with how decisions are being made at the top of world football. The letter from UEFA, AFC, and CONCACAF.

news.title: Austria’s football story: From Vienna’s gardens to the world stage
news.lede: Football has blossomed in the Alpine nation since being introduced by a gardener in the 19th century, producing a colourful array of teams, talent and even an NFL kicker. More than 130 years ago, English gardener James Black moved to Vienna to tend to the grounds of Baron Rothschild. The tales of football that he shared with colleagues laid the local seeds for the beautiful game, and in 1894 he was a founding member of First Vienna, the nation’s pioneering football club. From there, the sport grew quickly, with Vienna’s famous coffee house culture providing fertile ground for intellectuals and players alike to sit and discuss revolutionary footballing ideas.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa accused of breaking trust 'through deception'
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino was first elected in 2016. Fifa and its president Gianni Infantino have been accused of breaking trust "through deception" in an open letter issued by Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation. The letter, signed by the presidents and general secretaries, said recent controversy over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was fundamentally about "the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it". FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including the World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

news.title: Open letter to the football family
news.lede: Joint letter of AFC, CONCACAF and UEFA. Football is the world’s greatest shared passion. It belongs to no individual and no institution. It belongs to the players, the fans, the clubs, the Member Associations and every institution entrusted with safeguarding its future.
